Reason: The initial chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a cavitary lesion with an "air crescent" sign (white arrow) and adjacent pneumopericardium (black arrow), characteristic of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis. The follow-up X-ray (Figure 2) shows progression to a hydropneumopericardium (indicated by the air-fluid level at the black arrow), implying worsening pathology and the formation of a bronchopericardial fistula.
